about: Derived-check findings that are intentional. Each entry names its check id and finding key exactly as scripts/parity-check.mjs prints them, and says why. An entry that no longer matches anything is reported as stale: delete it.

entries.reason: Android never picks a language itself: the OS chooses among the app's values-<lang> resources (per-app language in system settings). The vectors are the rule for the webapp, the box pages and the website.

iOS never picks a language itself: the OS chooses among the app's localisations (Settings > App > Language). The vectors are the rule for the webapp, the box pages and the website, which negotiate Accept-Language / navigator.languages.
By the section's own notes the Mac's JSONEncoder writes an equivalent seed body, not the same bytes, so it doesn't assert this vector.

The Mac hosts on Virtualization.framework and never runs QEMU, so there is no QEMU stderr or WHPX memory failure to describe; its VZ errors are already plain. Only the Windows and Linux ports implement QemuFailure/qemu_failure.
Linux writes the seed through the Node CLI's appliance-provision, which packages/flagship-builder/tests/appliance.test.ts checks against this section.
Android's own dead-man reminder notification opens app/deadman/<server>; iOS's local reminder carries category deadman-affirm and serverDomain in userInfo instead of a link.

Only the canonical-bytes primitive exists on iOS and Android, pinned by their unit tests; no client issues, seals or unseals an ACME account-key grant yet (AGENTS.md open item 5). A webapp port would be dead code; port all three together with the sealing flow.
